questions.question_text:
A pattern begins at $7$ when $x=1$ and increases by $3$ each time $x$ increases by $1$.
Which table describes it?

options.why: Added $1$ each step instead of $3$.
Used the increase $3$ as the starting value instead of $7$.
Multiplied each $x$-value by $7$ instead of starting at $7$ and adding $3$ each step.

questions.question_text:
A pattern starts at $5$ when $x=1$ and increases by $2$ each time $x$ increases by $1$.
Which table describes it?

options.why: Increased $y$ by $1$ each step instead of the stated $2$.
Used the increase $2$ as the starting value and ignored the start of $5$.
Multiplied each $x$-value by $5$ instead of starting at $5$ and adding $2$ each step.

questions.question_text: Use the equation $y=4x+2$ to find the table for $x=0,1,2$.

options.why: Used $3x+2$ instead of $4x+2$, increasing by $3$ rather than $4$.
Swapped the coefficient and constant, using $2x+4$.
Subtracted $2$ instead of adding it, using $4x-2$.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1,xmax=4,ymin=-1,ymax=7,xtick={-1,0,1,2,3,4},ytick={0,2,4,6},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-0.3:3.4,samples=2] {-2*x+6};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.8pt] coordinates {(0,6) (1,4) (2,2) (3,0)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which table matches the displayed graph?

options.why: Read the line as falling by $1$ each step instead of $2$.
Read the points from right to left, reversing the $y$-values.
Treated the line as rising although the graph falls.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-1,xmax=4,ymin=-1,ymax=10,xtick={-1,0,1,2,3,4},ytick={0,2,4,6,8,10},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-0.3:3.4,samples=2] {2*x+3};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.8pt] coordinates {(0,3) (1,5) (2,7) (3,9)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which equation matches the displayed graph?

options.why: Swapped the increase of $2$ with the starting value $3$.
Read an increase of $1$ although the marked points rise by $2$.
Used the wrong sign for the value where the line crosses the $y$-axis.

questions.question_text: Use the equation $y=-4x+7$ to find the table for $x=0,1,2,3,4$.

options.why: Used $4x+7$, ignoring the negative coefficient.
Used $-4x-7$, subtracting the constant instead of adding it.
Swapped the coefficient and constant, using $7x-4$.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-2,xmax=5,ymin=-10,ymax=10,xtick={-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4,5},xticklabels={-2,-1,0,1,{},3,4,5},ytick={-10,-8,-6,-4,-2,0,2,4,6,8,10},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,<->,domain=-1.4:4.7,samples=2] {-3*x+5};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.8pt] coordinates {(-1,8) (0,5) (1,2) (2,-1) (3,-4) (4,-7)};\node[anchor=south,font=\small,fill=white,inner sep=1pt,yshift=3pt] at (axis cs:2,0) {$2$};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which equation matches the graph?

options.why: Used an increase of $3$ although the marked points decrease by $3$ for each increase of $1$ in $x$.
Read the value at $x=0$ as $-5$ instead of $5$.
Used the point's $y$-value $2$ at $x=1$ as the decrease, instead of finding the change from $5$ to $2$.

questions.solution_text:
$y=5$ when $x=0$.
From $x=0$ to $x=1$, $y$ changes from $5$ to $2$, a decrease of $3$.
$y=-3x+5$

questions.question_text: Find the equation represented by the table: $\begin{array}{c|ccccc}x&0&1&2&3&4\\\hline y&-5&-3&-1&1&3\end{array}$.

options.why: Used a decrease of $2$ although the table's $y$-values increase by $2$.
Used $5$ instead of $-5$ for the value at $x=0$.
Swapped the increase $2$ and the value $-5$ at $x=0$.

questions.solution_text:
$y$ increases by $2$ each time $x$ increases by $1$, and $y=-5$ when $x=0$.
$y=2x-5$
